summary: John R. B. Campbell works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD at Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman and Gary A. Tubb, alongside studies with traditional teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama.

John R. McRae specialized in Buddhist studies and Sinology, completing his PhD at Yale under Stanley Weinstein. He taught at Cornell and Indiana University, held professorships at Soka and Komazawa Universities, and chaired the Numata Center.

John Ronald Newman specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his PhD in 1987 from the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa and served as Assistant Professor of Asian Religions at New College of Florida.

John Ross Carter was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. After studying at King's College London and SOAS, he completed doctoral work at Harvard under Wilfred Cantwell Smith and served as a professor at Colgate University (~1972–2006).

John S. Strong is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed his degree at the University of Chicago under Frank E. Reynolds. He was a professor at Bates College (~1978–2020) and a Fulbright fellow in Ceylon.
John Shore was a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. Succeeding William Jones, he served as President of the Asiatic Society.

John Stratton Hawley is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, taught at Bowdoin College (~1974–1977), and became a professor at Columbia University around 1986.

John Taber is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen and Reiner Wiehl, later holding posts at Case Western Reserve University (~1984–1989) and the University of New Mexico.

John Thompson Platts was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Balliol College (~1880–1884) and served as Teacher of Persian at the University of Oxford (~1880–1904).

John Vincent Bellezza is a researcher in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He studied under Yungdrung Tenzin and Tshering Choephel and held an attested post at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences in 2014.

John W. Pettit specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed undergraduate studies at Haverford College, received doctoral supervision from Robert A. F. Thurman, and studied with Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche between 1985 and 1990.

John W. Schroeder specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Oregon under Don Levi and held teaching posts at Oregon, the College of Wooster, and St. Mary's College of Maryland.
John W. Spellman was an Indology and history scholar. He held academic posts at the University of Washington (~1964–1967) and served as a professor at the University of Windsor (~1967–2002).
John Wilson was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1819–1828) and served as President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1835–1842).

John Woodroffe was an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at University College, Oxford. He served as a judge at the Calcutta High Court (~1904–1922) and as Reader in Indian Law at Oxford (~1923–1930).

Jokai Hiraoka was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history who studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University. He was a professor at Otemae University (~1966–1989) and held a post at Shuchiin University.
Jon Kabat-Zinn works in religious studies and related fields. He earned his doctorate at MIT and founded and served as Professor of Medicine Emeritus at UMass Chan Medical School.

Jonardon Ganeri is a philosopher and Indologist who studied at Cambridge and Oxford under Bimal Krishna Matilal. He held posts at Nottingham, Liverpool, Sussex, Monash, NYU (~2013–2020), and the University of Toronto (~2020).

Jonathan A. Silk is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. After earning his doctorate at the University of Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez, he taught at Western Michigan, Yale, UCLA, and Leiden University.
Jonathan C. Gold is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He has taught at the University of Vermont, Drew University, and Princeton University.
